en.articles: Article 4-2, Paragraph 4, Item 2 of the Cabinet Order for Enforcement of the Customs Law; Article 1-7 of the Ordinance for Enforcement of the Customs Law
en.inputs: ① Hinge pin (subheading 7318.15) (raw materials of ①: iron bars (Chapter 72), inorganic chemicals (Chapter 28), organic chemicals (Chapter 29), water (Chapter 22)), ② U-nut (subheading 7318.16) (raw materials of ②: nut body (subheading 7318.16), friction ring (subheading 7318.21))
en.process: The above-mentioned raw material ① is manufactured in Japan through processes such as threading. The above-mentioned raw material ② is manufactured in Japan by crimping, etc., a nut body produced in Taiwan and a friction ring produced in Japan. Raw materials ① and ② are made into a set and packed in Japan, exported to the United States, and then re-imported into Japan.
en.reasoning: According to the information submitted by the applicant, the above-mentioned raw materials used in the production of the good in Japan are not recognized as wholly produced goods. The country of origin for the application of the WTO rate of duty for goods produced using materials that do not constitute wholly produced goods is, pursuant to Article 4-2, Paragraph 4, Item 2 of the Cabinet Order for Enforcement of the Customs Law, the country or territory where the good was produced through the working or processing specified in Article 1-7 of the Ordinance for Enforcement of the Customs Law. The processing of the good in Japan does not fall under "working or processing (including working or processing designated by the Directors-General of Customs) that results in the heading of the Annex to the Customs Tariff Law applicable to the good being different from the heading of the said Annex applicable to all raw materials or materials of the good (excluding goods originating in the country or territory where the good was produced)" as provided for in the said Ordinance. In addition, the good uses two or more types of raw materials, some of which originate outside Japan; however, among the raw materials used for the good, there are those that constitute important components that impart the essential character to the good and those that do not. According to Customs Law Basic Circular 68-3-5(5), when the manufacture of the good, viewed from the perspective of the raw material constituting the important component, does not fall under the working or processing prescribed in Article 1-7 of the Ordinance for Enforcement of the Customs Law, the country of origin prescribed in Article 4-2, Paragraph 4 of the Cabinet Order for Enforcement of the Customs Law is the last country or territory in which an act that brought about a substantial change and imparted a new characteristic was performed in the manufacture of the said raw material constituting the important component. Among the raw materials used in the production of the good, the important component that imparts the essential character to the good is ①. The processing of ① in Japan does not fall under the working or processing prescribed in Article 1-7 of the Ordinance for Enforcement of the Customs Law, and the last country where an act bringing about a substantial change and imparting a new characteristic was performed in the manufacture of ① is Japan. Therefore, since the country of origin of the good prescribed in Article 4-2, Paragraph 4 of the Cabinet Order for Enforcement of the Customs Law is Japan, the country of origin for the application of the WTO rate of duty is deemed to be the United States, which is the country of shipment, pursuant to Basic Circular Concerning Foreign Trade Statistics, etc., 6-2 and 7-2(2). Note that this advance ruling response is valid only for determining the origin regarding the application of the WTO rate of duty upon import customs clearance into Japan from the United States.

Pursuant to Article 4-2, Paragraph 4, Item 2 of the Cabinet Order for Enforcement of the Customs Tariff Act, the country of origin of goods produced using materials that do not constitute wholly obtained goods as provided for in Paragraph 4 of the said Article shall be the country or territory where the product was produced through processing or manufacturing as defined in Article 1-7 of the Regulation for Enforcement of the Customs Tariff Act. The processing of the product in Japan does not meet the criterion provided for in the said Regulation of "processing or manufacturing that results in the heading of the Customs Tariff Act Annexed Table under which the goods fall being different from the headings of the said Table under which all raw materials or materials (excluding goods whose origin is recognized as the country or territory where the goods were produced) fall (including processing or manufacturing designated by the Director-General of Customs)." According to Section 68-3-5(5) of the Basic Circular of the Customs Law, when the manufacturing of the product viewed from the raw materials constituting the essential components does not fall under the processing or manufacturing specified in Article 1-7 of the Regulation for Enforcement of the Customs Tariff Act, the country of origin provided for in Article 4-2, Paragraph 4 of the Cabinet Order for Enforcement of the Customs Tariff Act shall be the last country or territory where the act that brought about substantial transformation in the manufacture of the raw materials constituting said essential components and imparted new characteristics was performed. en.process:
The good is manufactured in South Korea through process (2) below, using the above raw material ① manufactured in Japan through process (1) below, some of ② to ⑤ procured in Japan and exported to South Korea, and some of ② and ④ procured in South Korea.
(1) Completion of ① through machining, etc., of the plastic block, which is the raw material for ①.
(2) Completion of the good through washing, assembly, inspection, etc., of ① through ⑤.
Remarks: This inquiry concerns the country of origin under Japan Customs Law Basic Circular 71-3-1 (False Indication of Origin, etc.).
en.reasoning:
Based on the information submitted by the applicant, the raw materials used in the production of the good in South Korea cannot be recognized as wholly obtained. Pursuant to Article 4-2, Paragraph 4, Item 2 of the Order for Enforcement of the Customs Law, the country of origin for goods produced using materials that are not wholly obtained is the country or territory where the good was produced through processing or manufacturing as prescribed in Article 1-7 of the Ordinance for Enforcement of the Customs Law.
The processing of the good in South Korea does not fall under "processing or manufacturing that results in the heading of the Harmonized System Tariff Schedule appended to the Customs Tariff Law applicable to the good being different from the heading of the same Schedule applicable to all the raw materials or materials (excluding goods whose country of origin is the country or territory where the good was produced) (including processing or manufacturing designated by the Director-General of Customs)" prescribed in the same Ordinance.
In addition, the good uses two or more types of raw materials, some of which originate outside of South Korea; however, among the raw materials used for the good, there are those that are essential components imparting the essential character to the good and those that are not.
Pursuant to Japan Customs Law Basic Circular 68-3-5(5), regarding the country of origin prescribed in Article 4-2, Paragraph 4 of the Order for Enforcement of the Customs Law, if the manufacture of the good viewed from the perspective of the raw material that is an essential component constitutes the processing or manufacturing prescribed in Article 1-7 of the Ordinance for Enforcement of the Customs Law, the country of origin is South Korea; otherwise, it is the last country or territory where an act resulting in a substantial transformation and imparting a new characteristic in the manufacture of the raw material that is such an essential component was performed.
Among the raw materials used in the production of the good, the essential component imparting the essential character to the good is ①.
The manufacture of the good in South Korea viewed from the perspective of ① does not constitute the processing or manufacturing prescribed in Article 1-7 of the Ordinance for Enforcement of the Customs Law, whereas the manufacture of ① in Japan is recognized as constituting the processing or manufacturing prescribed in Article 1-7 of the same Ordinance.
Therefore, the country of origin prescribed in Article 4-2, Paragraph 4 of the Order for Enforcement of the Customs Law for the good is recognized as Japan.
Note that this advance ruling response is valid solely for determining the country of origin prescribed in Article 4-2, Paragraph 4 of the Order for Enforcement of the Customs Law at the time of import customs clearance into Japan.
